summary: Perceived long-polling stalls from burst-quota collisions amplified by synchronous client retries
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent multi-second stalls when opening streaming responses in production. From the app viewpoint responses appear to freeze or time out for groups of requests, then recover after ~30–90s. The customer sees many client-side retries during the stalls which correlate to their synchronous retry logic.

Impact:
- NimbleHealth production integration experiences degradations on peak traffic windows (affects chat and batch scoring endpoints).
- User-facing timeouts and increased error rates; several support requests from their operations team.
- Estimated 12% increase in token cost due to duplicate retries during episodes.

Environment:
- Redwood dedicated pool (dedicated tier, reserved), us-east cluster.
- SDK: nimble-client-js v1.2.4 with default retry/backoff behavior (synchronous).
- Traffic pattern: short-lived spikes from scheduled background jobs overlapping user traffic between 09:00–10:30 UTC.

Observed behavior:
- Client logs show a pattern: initial request -> 429/queue hint or 503 in a minority -> client retries immediately (synchronous loop) -> cluster-side request queueing increases -> other requests stall for 20–80s (perceived hang).
- Server-side dashboards show transient bursts of queued requests at the API edge and a corresponding bump in rate-limiter drop metrics.

Expected behavior:
- Soft quota signals should not manifest as long-lived per-request stalls; intelligent queuing/priority should maintain short tail latency and avoid cascade amplification by customers' synchronous retries.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Configure quick-fire scheduled jobs that make 30 concurrent streaming requests over 2s window using the SDK v1.2.4 default retry settings.
2) Observe SDK retry behavior when a small percentage of initial requests are rejected or delayed by the rate-limiter.
3) Observe long-tail stalls on unrelated requests during the same minute.

Logs and traces (provided):
- Customer-provided request IDs: nh-prod-20260310-3a4b, nh-prod-20260310-3a9f, nh-prod-20260310-4c01.
- API edge logs indicate short 429 bursts followed by a sustained queue depth increase for ~60s.
- No GPU OOMs or model crashes in serving-runtime traces.

Notes:
- This ticket focuses on interaction between rate-limiter quota windows and synchronous client retry behavior (client-side amplification). We need to validate whether queueing at the gateway or an internal soft-window is the dominant factor.
impact: Customer-facing latency spikes during burst windows; duplicate retries increasing cost and error rates; affects production SLAs for NimbleHealth
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Trigger a 30-request burst in <5s using nimble-client-js v1.2.4. 2) Observe immediate retries on 429 responses. 3) Watch unrelated streaming requests experience long-tail stalls for ~20–90s.
logs_and_traces: Edge logs: short 429 run, then queue_depth metrics increased to 1200 for ~45–75s. Serving runtime traces show normal model throughput; no kernel failures. SDK traces show synchronous retry loops (no jitter).
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 14:20 UTC — Initial triage (Asha): correlated customer request IDs with api-gateway 429 spikes. Noted high queue_depth at the gateway during observed window.

2026-03-10 16:05 UTC — SRE (David): verified no GPU exhaustion; serving nodes within capacity. Observed rate-limiter drop → backlog at edge; backlog drained slowly due to synchronous retry amplification from the client SDK.

2026-03-11 09:30 UTC — Engineering (Mariana Silva): hypothesis: internal pacing window + lack of per-customer queue priority causes burst collisions; when many clients retry synchronously the backlog starves healthy in-flight requests.
2026-03-11 12:10 UTC — Ran controlled repro in staging with nimble-client-js v1.2.4: reproduced long-tail stalls when concurrency spikes >25 and retry jitter disabled.

2026-03-12 08:40 UTC — Temporary mitigation applied: lowered per-customer soft burst capacity on dedicated pool and enabled conservative retry-jitter suggestion in support reply. Observed reduction in tail by ~40% during subsequent controlled bursts.

2026-03-12 15:00 UTC — Follow-up: customer to deploy SDK patch to add jittered exponential backoff; engineering exploring edge-level backpressure signals (429 with Retry-After, or 202-queued) combined with client SDK best-practices doc.
comments: 2026-03-10 14:45 — Asha Patel (Support): Thanks for the report, NimbleHealth. We've captured the request IDs and started correlation. Can you confirm whether your job scheduler batches overlap with user traffic windows?
2026-03-10 15:02 — Carlos Ortega (NimbleHealth Ops): Yes — our cleanup/summary jobs run at 09:00–09:15 UTC and spike to ~200 TPS for a burst. We will throttle them if recommended.
2026-03-10 16:20 — David Lin (SRE): We saw gateway queue_depth jump in that window. No signs of model-level failure. We're investigating rate-limiter behavior and SDK retry pattern.

2026-03-11 12:40 — Mariana Silva (Engineering): Reproduced in staging. Short-term recommendation: add jitter and limit synchronous retries. Long-term: consider per-customer priority or burst-smoothing at edge.

2026-03-12 09:01 — Asha Patel (Support): Temporary config change applied to customer's pool to reduce burst allowance and reduce collision probability. Please roll out SDK change and report back over next 48h.
2026-03-12 10:23 — Carlos Ortega (NimbleHealth Ops): Deployed patched SDK with jittered backoff. Early metrics look better — error spikes reduced by ~60% in the next burst window.
2026-03-13 11:15 — David Lin (SRE): Ongoing: engineering evaluating a gateway-side soft-queue priority feature and better on-wire retry signals. Marking In Progress until follow-ups scheduled.
resolution:
Workaround: customer deployed SDK patch with jittered exponential backoff and reduced synchronous retries; platform temporarily tightened per-customer burst allowances on the dedicated pool.
Planned fix: engineering to prototype gateway burst-smoothing and richer retry signals (Retry-After/queued token) plus a support doc for ‘recommended retry patterns’ for customers on dedicated/private tiers.
Follow-up actions assigned to ENG-ops for prototype and support-doc authoring.
notes_for_followup:
- ENG: prototype gateway burst smoothing (owner: Mariana Silva).
- DOCS: publish 'SDK retry best practices' and add to onboarding for dedicated customers.
- CS: monitor NimbleHealth for 72h post SDK deployment and close if stable.
customer_feedback: 2026-03-13 09:00 — Carlos Ortega: After SDK patch and temporary pool change we saw a marked reduction in user-facing errors during the 09:00 window. Appreciate the quick turn-around.
